scope: step-by-step write: which byte at cl+0x109260 kills the client

sequence.step1: write 0x08 at cl+0 (clc.state) -- client alive, value kept
sequence.step2: write dword 2 at cl+0x109260 (netadr type) -- client DIED immediately

conclusion: cl+0x109260 is not a writable netadr type field. Writing a non-zero dword there makes the client dereference or dispatch through it and crash. Either the field is a pointer (and NET_CompareAdr receives the pointer value as the type), or the parser copies the six dwords from a different base than cl.
implications: the whole 'fill cl's netadr' route is dead -- the address the receive helper compares against is not (only) stored at cl+0x109260
the 0x5C231E copy at 0x5C2260 may read through an indirection: mov ebx,[0x331c0c8]; xor ebx,key; then [ebx+0x109260] could be a pointer to the real netadr rather than the netadr itself
next: dump the dword at cl+0x109260 as a pointer and follow it -- if it is non-null, the parser's six dwords come from there
if it is zero, the parser is comparing against a null pointer copied as the type, which is exactly why the comparison always fails and why writing 2 crashes (the client then treats 2 as a pointer)
that would mean the real fix is to make the connect path allocate/populate that pointer, i.e. run the game's own connect sequence
